data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of trained non-experts using a checklist is more reliable than a single expert's intuition because it converts a high-variance cognitive process (intuition) into a low-variance procedural process (protocol), specifically by eliminating 'expert blind spots' and fatigue-driven omissions.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The checklist is insufficiently granular to capture the critical failure modes of the task.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel suffers from 'groupthink' or social contagion, leading to collective blind ticking (compliance without verification).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The task requires synthesis of disparate data points that cannot be decomposed into a linear checklist.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The checklist acts as a variance-reduction filter. While the expert possesses higher peak accuracy, their reliability is compromised by stochastic omissions (forgetting a step) and cognitive tunneling (over-reliance on a familiar pattern). The panel's reliability stems from the additive probability of detection: the likelihood that at least one panelist flags a checklist item that the expert intuitively skipped.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
